context: Three independent sub-moves, each landable alone. For (1), pick the tools-side impl as canonical (it is test-covered), have resources call it, and diff the field sets explicitly -- any field dropped or gained in resource payloads is listed in the PR. For (2), extend PlatformRegistry metadata with required-credential fields; setup.py derives its display from it; CredentialManager behavior unchanged. For (3), relocate the interface consumed by benchbox.utils.config_interface so the edge points downward, then remove the ignore_imports entry so lint-imports enforces it forever.
description: Three review findings not covered by the other one-engine items. (1) benchbox/mcp/resources/registry.py duplicates the shaping logic of tools/discovery.py with slightly different field sets (_build_benchmark_detail at registry.py:69-103 vs _get_benchmark_info_impl; _build_platforms_list vs _list_platforms_impl) -- two parallel serializations of the same registry data; extract one shared serializer (core-side or a single mcp-internal module) consumed by both tools and resources. (2) benchbox/cli/commands/setup.py:126-193 hardcodes a per-platform table of descriptions and required credential field names, duplicating knowledge the platform adapters/registry own; move required-credential metadata into the platform registry and derive the table. (3) .importlinter:43 carries a live, ignored layering violation: benchbox.utils.config_interface -> benchbox.cli.config; invert the dependency (move the needed config seam into core or utils) and delete the ignore entry -- the .importlinter header (lines 9-12) states every ignore entry is a real violation that must not grow.

anti_patterns.dont: merge tool and resource serializers by adding a fields= parameter with per-caller branches
anti_patterns.instead: one canonical payload shape; resources are a projection of it
anti_patterns.why: per-caller branching is the same duplication with extra indirection

anti_patterns.dont: resolve the utils->cli violation by widening the ignore list or reshuffling module names
anti_patterns.instead: invert the dependency so the edge points from cli down, then delete the ignore entry
anti_patterns.why: the layering contract is the enforcement backbone of one-engine; papering over it defeats the program

deferrals.reason: Phase 1 adversarial review (2026-08-04) of merged PRs #1548-#1551. Deferred here rather than on one-engine-unify-statistics because that item is terminal and deferrals on done items are invisible; this item is the program's home for review findings the other items do not cover. The statistics unification is incomplete and its rung overclaims: rung 1 greps only benchbox/mcp and benchbox/cli, but its expected text asserts 'Statistics helpers exist only in benchbox/core'. Three implementations survive. (1) benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py::_build_latency_stats and _build_numeric_stats compute p90/p95/p99 by linear interpolation and stdev via statistics.pstdev (POPULATION, not sample), and this path feeds result bundles -- so a single bundle can carry two different definitions of the same field name. Measured on the 22 TPC-H fixture timings: core p95 200.0ms vs result_capture p95 199.0ms; core sample stdev 76.74 vs capture population stdev 74.97. (2) benchbox/core/vector_search/metrics.py::_percentile, linear interpolation. (3) benchbox/experimental/load_testing/analyzer.py::_percentile, floor-index. All three were out of scope for one-engine-unify-statistics, which sets do_not_modify benchbox/platforms/ and whose only_modify globs cover benchbox/core/results/ only. Follow-up must decide per site whether the field is the same statistic (migrate onto percentile_ms/sample_stdev_ms) or a deliberately different one (rename the field and document why), and must widen the verification grep beyond mcp+cli so it stops certifying a claim it does not check.
deferrals.summary: Unify the three percentile/stdev implementations that survived one-engine-unify-statistics
